The department has also urged farmers to adopt moisture conserving measures in their lands to avoid losing their produce during the expected dry spell. This is after the weatherman released its climate outlook for the short rains that show November (traditionally the peak of the OND rains) was unusually dry in most parts of the country. In addition, the forecast for December indicates that most parts of the country are likely to experience near-average to below-average rains. “The anticipated near-to-below rainfall in the ASALs is likely to reduce soil moisture, affecting crop growth and pasture availability. The near-to-below-normal rainfall, coupled with poor spatial distribution, may negatively affect crop production, over most parts, especially over parts of the Central and Eastern sectors of the country, including the Coastal region,” reads the forecast signed by KMD acting Director Edward Muriuki. “Farmers are advised to implement water conservation practices such as mulching, and monitor soil moisture closely. Livestock producers should prepare for potential water and fodder shortages by storing feed and ensuring water points are well-maintained.” In terms of rainfall distribution for the month of December, Nyeri is among counties expected to receive near to below or depressed rains. Generally, rainfall distribution, both in time and space for this month is expected to be poor in most parts of the country. “Highlands East of the Rift Valley and Central Kenya (Nairobi, Nyeri, Kirinyaga, Murang’a, Kiambu, Meru, Embu and Turkana and Tharaka Nithi counties will experience intermittent rainfall with some breaks during the (December) month. The total rainfall amounts are likely to be near to below the long-term average for December,” read the outlook. The counties of Siaya, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Nyamira, West Pokot, Bomet, Laikipia, Narok, Kericho, Bungoma and Busia are also expected to have rainfall to be near the long-term average amounts for the month of December. Communities living in the ASAL regions have been advised to come up with water preservation measures during the coming three months to avert a possible loss of their stock due to drought. In terms of health impacts, health officials have been advised to sensitize to the public the need to observe proper sanitation standards to avert outbreak of diseases. The Department has warned that owing to the below-average rainfall and dry conditions in most areas, the risk of heat stress and vector-borne disease is not a remote possibility. “Public health advisories should emphasize proper hydration, safe food handling, and vector control measures such as mosquito net use and environmental sanitation. In areas where occasional rainfall may lead to localized flooding, stagnant water may create favourable conditions for the spread of vector-borne diseases. Conversely, in regions experiencing extended dry and dusty spells-particularly in the northern parts of the country –there may be an increased risk of respiratory and diarrhoea diseases due to compromised hygiene and water scarcity,” stated KMD. In October this year, KMD had warned of heavy rains in selected parts of the country during the October –November –December rains. Some of the areas that were expected to experience heavy downpour included those in the Lake Victoria Basin, the Rift Valley, the Highlands West of Rift Valley, West of Rift Valley and Highlands East of the Rift Valley according to the weather advisory released on October 22 2025. Among counties that had been put on high alert from the expected downpour included Kisumu, Nyeri, Bomet, Isiolo, Nairobi, Turkana, Mandera, Kajiado, Tharaka Nithi, Baringo and Murang’a. Overall, a total of 39 counties had been placed on high alert. “Rainfall currently affecting parts of the Lake Basin, the Rift Valley and the Highlands west of Rift Valley is expected to intensify to more than 30mm in 24 hours and spread to the Highlands of Rift Valley including Nairobi and parts of Southeastern lowlands on Thursday 23 October 2025.This is likely to mark the onset of the Short Rains Season (OND)2025 over several parts of the country expect over parts of Southern lowlands and the coastal region as indicated in the OND 2025 Forecast,” read the statement, signed by then KMD acting Director Kennedy Thiong’o. People residing in the listed regions had been advised on the need to take precautionary measures during the rainy season to avert possible water related catastrophes. The advisory was also shared with relevant emergency response agencies including the Presidency, Kenya Red Cross, National Disaster Management Operations Center and National Disaster Management Unit, Media and Council of Governors for proper preparedness and response in incase of disaster. “Flood waters may appear in places where it has not rained heavily, especially downstream. People are advised to avoid driving through or walking in moving water, open fields and not to shelter under trees and near grilled windows to minimize exposure to lightning strikes. People in landslide prone areas especially in the slopes of Aberdare ranges, Mt Kenya and other sloppy areas over the western region should be on high alert,” continued the advisory. The regions bordering the Highlands West of Rift Valley, the Lake Basin, the Central Rift Valley, the Northwest and most parts of the Highlands East of the Rift Valley were expected to receive near to above average rainfall. “The outlook for October 2025 indicates that the Highlands west of the Rift Valley, the Lake Victoria Basin, the Central and South Rift Valley, the Northwest, most parts of the Highlands east of the Rift Valley (including Nairobi County), and isolated areas in Marsabit are likely to experience near to above –average rainfall. In contrast, most of the Southeastern lowlands, the southern coast, a few areas of the Highlands east of the Rift Valley, and isolated areas of the Northeast and much of the Coastal region are expected to receive near to below-average rainfall,” continued the update. Nyeri., Murang’a, Embu, Meru, Nairobi, Kiambu, Tharaka Nithi and parts of Laikipia were among counties expected to receive rains near to above the long-term average for the month.

Nandi intensifies fight against gender violence following alarming statistics. Nandi County has intensified efforts to combat Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and femicide following revelations that 38.4 per cent of women aged between 15 and 49 years have experienced physical violence at some point in their lives, placing the county fifth nationally in the prevalence of physical violence against women. The statistics, released during a sensitisation meeting of the Nandi County Gender Sector Working Group in Kapsabet, have prompted stakeholders to call for urgent, coordinated interventions involving the National Government, County Government, religious institutions, civil society organisations, community leaders and residents. According to the findings presented during the meeting, Nandi ranks behind Kakamega, Uasin Gishu, Elgeyo Marakwet and Vihiga counties in reported cases of physical violence against women. The county also recorded 16 reported femicide cases in 2023, ranking sixth nationally, while 20 cases were reported in 2024, placing it tenth nationally. Participants said the statistics highlight the need for strengthened prevention strategies, improved survivor support services and greater public awareness to curb the rising cases of violence against women and girls. Nandi County Commissioner Wilberforce Kilonzo said addressing GBV and femicide requires collective responsibility and sustained public engagement, noting that government agencies alone cannot eliminate the vice. He said the National Government has continued to use Huduma Mashinani forums across the county’s six sub-counties to educate residents on Gender-Based Violence, teenage pregnancy, child protection and other social challenges affecting communities. Kilonzo urged government agencies, faith-based organisations, civil society groups, schools and community leaders to intensify public awareness campaigns to encourage victims to report cases promptly and help transform attitudes that perpetuate violence. “The fight against Gender-Based Violence requires the active participation of every stakeholder. Through Huduma Mashinani forums, we are continuously sensitising communities on GBV, teenage pregnancy and other social issues, but more partnerships are needed if we are to eliminate these crimes,” he said. County Director of Gender George Ondonga said the meeting was convened to familiarise members of the Gender Sector Working Group with the findings and recommendations of the Gender Technical Working Group on GBV and Femicide and to develop interventions tailored to the county’s needs. Ondonga challenged members of the working group to move beyond policy discussions and become ambassadors against GBV within their respective institutions and communities. “Every member of the Gender Sector Working Group has a responsibility to become an ambassador in the fight against GBV and femicide by taking prevention messages to the grassroots,” he said. Teenage pregnancy also emerged as a major concern during the meeting. Stakeholders heard that 17 per cent of girls aged between 15 and 19 years in Nandi County have experienced pregnancy, with Aldai Sub-county recording the highest prevalence at 23 per cent. Participants said teenage pregnancy, school dropout, harmful cultural practices, alcohol and substance abuse and sexual violence are interconnected challenges requiring integrated interventions involving parents, schools, health providers and community leaders. To strengthen prevention and response, stakeholders recommended increased funding for GBV programmes, expanded public sensitisation campaigns and stronger collaboration among government institutions, faith-based organisations, civil society and community structures. They further proposed convening a county summit bringing together the Council of Elders, senior religious leaders, elected leaders and civil society organisations to develop a unified strategy for combating GBV and femicide. The meeting also resolved to mobilise resources from both the National and County Governments for the construction of a Gender-Based Violence Recovery Centre at Kapsabet County Referral Hospital. Kilonzo and Ondonga committed to convening a consultative meeting with relevant leaders and partners to explore funding options for the proposed facility. The planned recovery centre would provide temporary shelter, psychosocial counselling, legal assistance, medical care and referral services for survivors, particularly those who may face further danger if they return home immediately after reporting abuse. Stakeholders urged the National Government to prioritise Nandi County in its plan to establish a GBV Recovery Centre in every county, citing the county’s high prevalence of physical violence and increasing femicide cases. The meeting also examined the role of cultural practices in shaping behaviour among young people. Participants called on community elders to review the teachings offered during initiation ceremonies to ensure they promote respect for parents, teachers, women and children while discouraging violence, discrimination and harmful cultural norms. They observed that initiation rites should reinforce positive values, responsibility and peaceful coexistence instead of perpetuating attitudes that encourage abuse or gender inequality. Schools and colleges were identified as critical platforms for preventing GBV through education and early intervention. Stakeholders recommended integrating anti-GBV sensitisation programmes into learning institutions by involving teachers, counsellors and peer educators while using digital platforms, videos and other educational materials to create awareness among learners. Recognising the importance of engaging men and boys in preventing violence, the meeting proposed establishing male engagement committees at county and sub-county levels to champion positive masculinity and support community awareness campaigns. Participants also resolved to strengthen GBV referral pathways, improve coordination among duty bearers involved in prevention, reporting and case management, and promote the use of social media to reach more people with anti-GBV messages. They discouraged the use of Kipkaa, a traditional alternative dispute resolution mechanism, to handle GBV cases, saying criminal offences should be reported to law enforcement agencies and prosecuted through the justice system. The meeting further recommended holding standalone anti-GBV public barazas to provide sufficient time for focused discussions on prevention, survivor support and available reporting mechanisms. Stakeholders urged members of the public to report cases of sexual and gender-based violence promptly and called for a harmonised reporting system to improve coordination among government agencies and ensure survivors receive timely assistance. The sensitisation meeting brought together 20 members of the Nandi County Gender Sector Working Group drawn from the National Government Administration, Kenya Police Service, Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, State Department for Gender and Affirmative Action, faith-based organisations and other partner institutions. The participants concluded by reaffirming their commitment to strengthening prevention, survivor protection, public awareness, coordination and accountability in the fight against Gender-Based Violence and femicide, expressing optimism that sustained collaboration among all stakeholders would help reverse the alarming trends and create safer communities across Nandi County. By Geoffrey Satia

Turkana intensifies preparations for Community Conservancy Board elections. The Turkana County Government, in partnership with the Northern Rangelands Trust (NRT), has intensified public engagement activities in Letea, Turkana West Sub-County, to prepare residents for the election of members to the Community Conservancy Board. The initiative seeks to strengthen community participation in natural resource management while laying the foundation for effective governance of the proposed conservancy. The ongoing programme includes stakeholder consultations, community capacity building and the development of a Community Conservancy Action Plan aimed at equipping residents with the knowledge required to participate meaningfully in the election process. The exercise is being led by County Director of Natural Resources Pauline Ng’oli and NRT Team Lead Moses Kinapu in collaboration with local administrators, community leaders and other stakeholders. Speaking during the public engagement forum, Ng’oli said the process is intended to ensure the Community Conservancy Board is established in accordance with the law and begins operating on a strong institutional foundation. “We have chosen to work closely with administrative structures, local institutions, community leaders and residents to establish a board that will effectively manage the proposed conservancy,” she said. Ng’oli noted that involving local communities from the outset would enhance transparency, accountability and community ownership of conservation programmes. Residents welcomed the initiative, saying the training had increased their understanding of the community conservancy model and prepared them to elect capable leaders. “We now have a better understanding of the community conservancy model and how it operates. As a community, we feel ready for the elections,” said Letea resident Mariao Peyonon. NRT Team Lead Moses Kinapu emphasised the importance of conducting free, fair and transparent elections, noting that residents could choose board members through either a secret ballot or consensus, depending on what the community agreed. Kinapu cited successful examples from conservancies such as Nasalot, where community conservancy boards have strengthened natural resource management, promoted environmental conservation and improved livelihoods. The County Government and NRT said they are promoting the community conservancy model in Letea and other parts of Turkana West to enhance environmental conservation, encourage community participation in natural resource governance and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for local residents. By Peter Gitonga

Coastal residents urged to back government development agenda. Cabinet Secretaries Salim Mvurya (Youth Affairs, Creative Economy and Sports) and Hassan Joho (Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs) are actively urging residents in the coastal region to support the national development agenda. The two leaders emphasized the importance of community collaboration with the national government in driving sustainable economic activity, job creation, and the equitable use of public resources. Mvurya and Joho, accompanied by a host of local leaders, were speaking at Ronald Ngala grounds in Mombasa County during a meet-the-people engagement. They were accompanied by Mombasa Governor Abdulswamad Shariff Nassir, Senator Mohamed Faki; MPs Mohamed Machele (Mvita), Badi Twalib (Jomvu), Rashid Bedzimba (Kisauni), Mishi Mboko (Likoni) and Principal Secretary for Youth Affairs, Fikirini Jacobs. Ministers Mvurya and Joho, who are past two-term governors of Kwale and Mombasa, respectively, said policy continuity was critical to sustaining economic reforms, improving security and delivering long-term prosperity. The two defended the Kenya Kwanza administration’s record on regional equity, saying development was now being shared fairly across the country. “We want the people to continue supporting the bottom-up economic growth strategy of the national government,” said Mvurya. CS Mvurya reaffirmed the National Government’s commitment to creating opportunities for the youth to enable them to participate meaningfully in the country’s socio-economic development. Mvurya cited the Sh5 billion National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) project, which he noted is a bold intervention that will foster socio-economic stability in the long run. He said the NYOTA project, championed by the national government, is potentially a ‘panacea to the widespread youth unemployment’ and associated social ills in the country. Mvurya said the government will continue upskilling young people and creating an enabling environment where they can thrive. He said they will continue to crisscross the coastal counties of Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi, Lamu, Taita Taveta and Tana River with elected leaders to promote peace and unity ahead of the 2027 general elections. Mvurya said they will continue engaging coastal residents to back the government development agenda on account of its commitment to advancing national development through sustained investment in priority sectors aimed at strengthening service delivery. On his part, CS Joho expressed the government’s commitment to accelerating meaningful development and expanding opportunities for the youth. He said the meet-the-people forums are focused on strengthening infrastructure, expanding economic opportunities, empowering the youth and enhancing service delivery while underscoring the importance of sustained public participation in shaping the development agenda. “We urge coastal residents to continue supporting the national government in its endeavor to undertake transformative development programmes in every corner of the country,” said Joho. Joho urged residents not to gamble with their future in the forthcoming 2027 general polls, warning that a wrong electoral decision could set back an entire generation. He said major infrastructure and economic projects in the coastal region include the Dongo Kundu Bypass (Mombasa), Mwache Multipurpose Dam (Kwale), LAPSSET Corridor (Lamu), and the proposed Mombasa-Nairobi expressway. “All these mega projects are geared toward transforming regional trade, water security, and transportation,” he said. Joho said the government will continue implementing programmes that promote inclusive development and enhance the quality of life for the citizenry. Governor Nassir urged the youth to avoid challenges such as drug and substance abuse, which he decried as a worrying reality affecting the society. The coastal county boss urged the youth to shun drug abuse and criminal activities to protect their personal health and secure a prosperous future. By Hussein Abdullahi

Maalim urges Northern Kenya residents to register as voters. Mandera Deputy Governor Dr. Ali Maalim has called on residents of Northern Kenya to register as voters, saying higher voter registration will strengthen the region’s political influence ahead of the 2027 General Election. Speaking during an Annual General Meeting (AGM) of a school in Mandera, Dr. Maalim urged all eligible residents to take advantage of the ongoing Enhanced Continuous Voter Registration (ECVR) exercise being conducted by the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC). He appealed to residents of Mandera, Wajir, Garissa, Marsabit, Isiolo, Tana River and Turkana counties to register in large numbers, saying the pastoralist region must fully demonstrate its electoral strength. “We want everybody to take advantage of the voter registration exercise. I urge all the people of Mandera and Northern Kenya to ensure they register as voters. As pastoralist communities, we must demonstrate our numbers and ensure our voices are heard,” said Dr. Maalim. The Deputy Governor said increased voter registration would enhance the region’s voice in national decision-making and ensure its interests are well represented in future political processes. Dr. Maalim also reaffirmed his political support for President William Ruto, saying the region remained firmly behind the Head of State ahead of the 2027 polls. “Our direction is very clear. We are supporting President William Ruto, and we are not wavering on that position,” he said. His remarks come as the IEBC continues with Voter Registration exercise across the country to enlist new voters before the next General Election. According to IEBC statistics, 97,859 new voters have been registered across the North Eastern region during the exercise. Garissa leads with 24,575 new voters, followed by Marsabit (23,267), Wajir (21,171), Mandera (18,214) and Isiolo (10,632). Nationally, the commission has registered 2,345,476 new voters during the 30-day mass voter registration campaign, bringing the total number of newly registered voters since continuous registration resumed in September 2025 to 2,612,725. The IEBC, together with political leaders and civic organisations, continues to encourage eligible Kenyans, especially youth and first-time voters, to register and participate in the country’s democratic process. By Adan Mohamed

Tharaka Nithi plans constituency museums to preserve culture for future generations. The Tharaka Nithi County Government will establish small museums in each constituency to preserve and promote the county’s cultural heritage, Governor Muthomi Njuki has announced. Speaking during the closing ceremony of a two-day Chuka Igambang’ombe Cultural Festival at Kaanwa Chiefs’ Camp, Njuki said the museums will showcase cultural artifacts, traditions and the history of communities across the county while serving as learning centres for residents, students and visitors. The governor directed the County Department of Culture to allocate funds for the initiative in the next county budget, saying the project is intended to safeguard the county’s rich heritage for future generations. “We must not allow our culture to disappear because it defines who we are. Our children should know their traditions and heritage,” Njuki said, expressing concern that many young people have limited knowledge of their cultural roots. He called on parents, elders and community leaders to take a leading role in passing cultural values, customs and traditions from one generation to another. Njuki said the county government would continue supporting community-based organisations, artists and cultural groups to strengthen efforts aimed at preserving and promoting local traditions. He noted that cultural festivals provide important platforms for celebrating identity, promoting unity and educating younger generations about their heritage. The governor also announced that the county’s flagship Ura Gate Cultural Festival will be held in August, with the exact date to be communicated later. He said the event will bring together communities from across Tharaka Nithi to celebrate the county’s cultural diversity through performances, exhibitions and traditional activities. Commending the success of the Chuka Igambang’ombe Cultural Festival, Njuki said the large turnout and colourful performances reflected residents’ commitment to preserving their cultural heritage. He praised the 25 cultural dance groups, artists, organisers and residents who participated in the festival for keeping traditional practices alive and encouraging cultural appreciation among young people. The governor also appealed to residents to protect wildlife by avoiding the killing of wild animals, saying conservation is essential in preserving Kenya’s natural heritage for future generations. On leadership, Njuki cautioned residents against embracing politics based on regional or clan interests, saying no constituency can elect leaders without support from others. Instead, he urged voters to evaluate leaders based on their development record, integrity and commitment to serving all residents equally, regardless of their place of origin. Maara Member of Parliament Kareke Mbiuki said annual cultural festivals play a vital role in preserving traditions while strengthening community identity, unity and social cohesion. Mbiuki commended the county government for supporting cultural groups and organising constituency cultural festivals, saying the initiative would help safeguard Tharaka Nithi’s rich cultural heritage for generations to come. By Christine Ngitori and Glory Kiende

Groundnut business sustains Kericho trader’s family. As formal employment opportunities remain limited, many Kenyans are increasingly turning to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to earn a living, support their families and contribute to local economic growth. Across towns and trading centres, small businesses continue to provide livelihoods for thousands of entrepreneurs, proving that modest investments, combined with determination and hard work, can transform lives and create sustainable sources of income. For 45-year-old Daniel Langat, a groundnut trader operating in Kericho town, selling roasted groundnuts has become more than just a business. It is the enterprise that has sustained his family, educated his children and given him hope for a better future over the past decade. Originally from Olenguruone in Kuresoi South Constituency, Nakuru County, Langat runs his business near the Jumbo area and opposite Kericho County Referral Hospital, serving commuters, traders, patients, visitors and residents throughout the day. The father of five says the business has enabled him to meet household expenses, pay rent and educate his children, with his first-born expected to complete Form Four this year. Langat’s entrepreneurial journey began after financial challenges forced him to drop out of school after completing Class Eight. Unable to continue with his education because his family could not afford school fees, he ventured into various informal jobs in search of a reliable source of income. Before settling on groundnut trading, he sold pineapples, hawked soap and worked for other people while learning the basics of running a business. From those experiences, he realised that roasted groundnuts offered a more dependable market. Compared to some of the other products he had sold, customers rarely complained about quality, while demand remained relatively steady throughout the year. Nearly 10 years later, the business has grown into his family’s main source of livelihood. Langat sells roasted groundnuts in packages ranging from Sh10 to Sh50 and above, making the product affordable to customers from different income groups. On slow business days, he earns between Sh1,500 and Sh2,000, while on good days his earnings exceed Sh3,000. He attributes his progress to consistency, discipline and patience rather than the size of his business. “Many people believe success only comes from big businesses, but I have learnt that consistency is more important than size. Every packet I sell brings me a step closer to my goals, and that is what keeps me going despite the daily challenges,” said Langat. Despite the gains, he acknowledges that operating a small business comes with uncertainties. Customer numbers fluctuate from one day to another, making it difficult to predict daily income. He says some days record brisk sales while others attract only a handful of customers, requiring resilience and careful financial planning to remain in business. “Business has its ups and downs. There are days when customers are few and sales are low, but giving up has never crossed my mind. Every new day presents another opportunity, and I have learnt that persistence is what keeps a business alive,” he added. Langat is also an active member of Africa Gospel Church (AGC) Immanuel in Kericho town, where he draws encouragement to remain focused on his business and family responsibilities. Looking ahead, he hopes to expand the enterprise through increased savings and eventually diversify into other income-generating ventures to improve his family’s living standards. He believes access to affordable financing would enable many small-scale traders to increase stock, improve their businesses and create employment opportunities for others. Langat has appealed to the government to establish more designated trading spaces for small-scale entrepreneurs and expand access to affordable loans and grants to help traders grow their enterprises. He further urged the government to introduce empowerment programmes targeting entrepreneurs above the youth age bracket, noting that while several initiatives support young people, many older business owners also struggle to access affordable capital despite operating viable enterprises. According to Langat, strengthening MSMEs through financial support, training and better trading infrastructure would not only improve household incomes but also contribute significantly to local economic development. He also encouraged aspiring entrepreneurs not to wait indefinitely for formal employment but to take advantage of available opportunities, however small, while remaining committed to disciplined financial management. “No work is too small if it is honest. Start with the little capital you have, remain disciplined and save consistently. Do not underestimate any business because what matters is how you organise and manage it. With patience, commitment and wise planning, a small enterprise can grow into a business that supports a family and even creates jobs for others,” he said. As more Kenyans embrace self-employment, MSMEs continue to play a vital role in reducing unemployment and strengthening local economies. Businesses such as Langat’s demonstrate how resilience, prudent management and determination can turn small ventures into reliable sources of income, supporting families while contributing to economic growth and community development. By Faith Chelang’at and Monica Irua

Tharaka Nithi rolls out projects to boost trade. The Tharaka Nithi County Government has unveiled a multisectoral development programme for Kaanwa Trading Centre in Mariani Ward, featuring road infrastructure, a modern market,improved healthcare and coffee revitalization to spur economic growth and improve livelihoods. Governor Muthomi Njuki announced the projects while launching the Kaanwa market roads paving project, saying the investments are part of the county’s broader strategy to modernise trading centres and improve access to essential services. He said the county government will pave roads within Kaanwa market to enhance accessibility and mobility, noting that the trading centre falls under Kathwana Municipality and will benefit from the municipality’s development initiatives. “Good town infrastructure, especially roads and markets, is a key driver of economic growth and would restore the dignity of our traders,” the Governor said. Njuki further announced that the county government will construct staircases for all shops in the market to improve accessibility, safety, and the general outlook of the trading centre. The Governor also revealed that rehabilitation of the MitheruKaanwa road is underway to enhance connectivity, ease transportation and facilitate movement of goods and services. On agriculture, the Governor urged farmers in Mariani Ward to embrace coffee farming, saying research had confirmed that the crop can perform well in the area. Research has shown that coffee can thrive here, and we will continue investing in the sector to unlock its full potential,” Njuki said. By Dickson Mwiti and Christine Ngitori

Goverment launches hassle-free mobile ID cards enrollment exercise. By H, KNA The State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services has launched a hassle-free mobile enrollment exercise for the issuance of national identity (ID) cards dubbed Usajili Mashinani. The Usajili Mashinani is a people-centred initiative designed to reduce barriers to registration and ensure citizens fully benefit from the ongoing national government projects and social services across the country. Local opinion leaders have been urged to support the new initiative by encouraging all eligible people to show up for enrolment. State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services Principal Secretary (PS) Dr. Belio Kipsang says the new registration drive seeks to make the vital document accessible to all Kenyans, especially those residing in difficult-to-access areas. Dr. Kipsang urged eligible citizens to take advantage of this new ID campaign which will be characterized by mobile registration efforts. The PS urged administrators to support and expedite legitimate applications, provide accurate registration data, and support public awareness, noting that access to identification is a constitutional right and critical to socio-economic inclusion. “All registration officers are expected to uphold the highest standards of professionalism and discipline as corruption will attract punitive measures,” he said. The PS encouraged citizens to acquire national IDs to access government services, highlighting that over 400,000 users access the eCitizen platform daily, all of whom require a valid ID. Dr. Kipsang said to enhance mobile registration, the government has deployed 100 live capture machines, with additional units set to be rolled out nationwide to further intensify registration across the country. The initiative uses mobile units to target remote areas and pastoralist communities with a goal to reducing the time it takes to receive ID cards to a week. “This live capture technology will allow on-the-spot registration of citizens in remote areas with data transmitted real-time for processing within the shortest time possible,” said Dr. Kipsang. The PS commended chiefs and assistant chiefs for their continued efforts in the registration of persons. He said the government will use the ID cards scheme as a ‘reliable comprehensive data base’ to plan for the present and future generations. “The government is working overdrive to ensure that no Kenyan who turns 18 years and above is denied access to their rightful identity,” he said. He says the current identity cards issuance effort, specifically targets Kenyans residing in far-flung areas, where national registration offices do not exist. The PS was speaking in Hola town, Tana River county, accompanied by heads of directorates from the State Department, where he led a sensitization programme, engaging National Government Administrative Officers (NGAOs) on the Revised National ID registration guidelines. The sensitization focused on familiarizing administrators with the revised framework and emphasized the importance of expanding mobile registration outreach to ensure all eligible Kenyans access identification services. Dr. Kipsang called on National Government Administrative Officers(NGAOs) to strengthen grassroots sensitization, ahead of the upcoming 10-day intensive mobile registration exercise across Tana River county, reinforcing Usajili Mashinani as a key driver of inclusive service delivery. The PS said to accelerate the process, the government has eliminated mandatory intensive vetting for border counties placing such responsibility on local chiefs and their assistants to verify new applicants. He said the mandatory vetting in border counties was abolished by President Dr. William Ruto in May 2024, as it has placed many hurdles and created unnecessary bureaucracy denying many vital documents. Dr. Kipsang said similar sensitization engagements have been successfully conducted in Kilifi, Kwale, Taita Taveta, and Mombasa counties, strengthening grassroots coordination and delivery of registration services. He encouraged citizens to take advantage of this opportunity to obtain their ID cards, which are essential for participating in national activities including the upcoming 2027 general elections. “Usajili Mashinani is an initiative that will ensure that every eligible citizen is registered, empowering Kenyans to participate in the country’s growth and development,” he said. He said his office is determined to work towards ensuring that every Kenyan is accounted for and has access to their rightful identity and take part in nation building. The PS said that the government remains dedicated to preserving the integrity of Kenyan citizenship for ‘national pride and security’. “National government officials should ensure that the ID card issuance process to capture the populace proceeds smoothly in their areas of jurisdiction,” said the PS, adding that ID cards has a pervasive impact on every facet of the socio-economic fabric of the nation. ID cards serve as a critical document required for obtaining a taxpayer identification number, opening a bank account and applying for jobs, voters card and passport. They are also required for accessing social protection services including the Inua Jamii Cash Transfer programme for vulnerable populations such as the elderly.

Tinderet farmers face poor maize harvest due to drought. Farmers in Tinderet Sub County are facing the prospect of one of the poorest maize harvests in recent years after erratic rainfall disrupted crop development, raising concerns over food shortages, rising maize prices and declining household incomes. Agricultural experts estimate that maize production in the sub-county could decline by between 30 and 40 per cent compared to a normal season, following prolonged dry spells experienced during critical stages of crop growth, particularly flowering and grain filling. Tinderet Sub County normally produces between 90,000 and 100,000 bags of maize annually, but this season’s output is projected to drop to between 55,000 and 65,000 bags due to moisture stress affecting thousands of hectares under maize production. Agronomist Peter Kiprono said inconsistent rainfall patterns had significantly reduced the yield potential of maize farms across the area. “The rainfall distribution was highly unreliable. While some locations received heavy downpours, they were followed by prolonged dry spells that stressed the maize crop at the most critical growth stages. We expect yields to decline sharply across most parts of the sub-county,” he said. According to the Ministry of Agriculture, maize is grown on nearly 18,000 hectares in Tinderet Sub County every year and contributes more than 60 per cent of household food requirements. However, field assessments have shown that many farms have been affected by moisture stress, with farmers reporting stunted crops, poorly filled cobs and reduced yields. In Songhor-Soba, Chemilil-Chemase and Kapchorua wards, farmers who expected to harvest between 20 and 25 bags of maize per acre now anticipate collecting only eight to 15 bags per acre. Farmer John Keter from Meteitei said the poor harvest would negatively affect his family’s food security and income. “We invested heavily in certified seeds and fertiliser, but the rains failed us. Instead of harvesting about 120 bags from my six-acre farm, I expect barely 60 bags. That means I will have to buy maize before the end of the year,” he said. Agricultural economist Jane Chebet warned that climate variability had become a major threat to food production in the region, urging farmers to embrace climate-smart farming practices. “The traditional rainfall seasons are becoming increasingly unpredictable. Farmers should adopt drought-tolerant maize varieties, water harvesting technologies and conservation agriculture to minimise production losses. Diversifying into crops such as beans, sorghum and millet will also improve resilience,” she said. The expected decline in production is likely to affect maize prices, with consumers facing higher costs due to reduced supply. A 90-kilogramme bag currently retailing between Sh4,800 and Sh5,200 could rise to between Sh6,000 and Sh6,500 later in the year if production shortages persist. Economists said reduced harvests would also affect household incomes because many farmers depend on maize sales to meet essential needs such as school fees, medical expenses and other family obligations. With fewer bags available for sale, households are expected to experience reduced disposable incomes, affecting spending power and local economic activities. Livestock farmers are also likely to feel the impact of the poor maize harvest as reduced availability of maize stalks could create shortages of animal feed during the dry season. This may force farmers to purchase supplementary feeds at higher costs. Food security advocate Grace Jepkemboi called for urgent measures to support vulnerable households and strengthen resilience among farmers. “Families that depend almost entirely on maize for food will be the hardest hit. We need greater investment in irrigation, climate-smart farming, timely weather information and crop diversification to safeguard food security,” she said. Stakeholders said increased investment in irrigation, access to reliable weather forecasts, improved extension services and promotion of drought-resistant crops would help farmers cope with changing weather patterns. Nationally, maize accounts for more than 65 per cent of Kenya’s staple food consumption, with the average Kenyan consuming about 98 kilogrammes annually. A significant decline in production from major maize-growing regions such as Tinderet could therefore contribute to supply shortages and increased prices across the country. By Sammy Mwibanda

Garissa Public Service Board fully constituted after members sworn in. The Garissa County Public Service Board has been fully reconstituted following the swearing-in of three new members, paving the way for the board to resume full operations and strengthen public service management in the county. The ceremony, held at the Garissa County headquarters, was presided over by Garissa Chief Magistrate Thomas Mwangi, who administered the oath of office to Abdikadir Gure Farah, Naima Hassan Farah and Muhumed Abdi Oyow. The appointments restore the board to full membership after vacancies arose following the expiry of the terms of three former members. Garissa Governor Nathif Jama, accompanied by Deputy Governor Abdi Dagane, congratulated the new members and urged them to begin their duties immediately, noting that residents expect a fully functional board capable of improving service delivery. The Governor called on the board, led by Chairman Ahmed Abdirahman, to strengthen public service management, promote professionalism and ensure the county maintains an efficient and stable workforce. He further challenged the board to support measures aimed at containing the county wage bill while ensuring recruitment is based on merit and transparency. Jama said a professional public service is essential for maintaining continuity in government operations, even during periods of political transition. The Governor also urged the board to undertake payroll cleansing to eliminate irregularities and ensure that only qualified personnel are employed in the county public service. He said the exercise would enhance accountability, improve efficiency and promote quality service delivery to residents. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by County Commissioner John Cheruiyot, County Secretary Mohamud Mursal, Members of the County Assembly led by Sankuri MCA Abdirahman Mohamed, Township Sub-County Administrator Shaiya Hambe, as well as family members and friends of the newly appointed board members. By Mohamed Dahir

Government expresses optimism over economic growth. National Treasury Principal Secretary Dr. Chris Kiptoo has assured Kenyans that the country’s economy remains stable, saying the government has made significant progress in restoring macroeconomic stability despite global economic shocks experienced over the past few years. Speaking in Gichugu, Kirinyaga County, Dr. Kiptoo said the economy had faced major external challenges from 2022, including the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war, which triggered high inflation, depreciation of the Kenya shilling and increased pressure on public debt management. “The external factors manifested in a very big way. Domestic prices went up, inflation rose to almost 9.6 per cent, the shilling came under a lot of pressure and we experienced challenges in managing our debt,” Dr. Kiptoo said. He noted that through deliberate government interventions over the last three years, the economy has steadily recovered. “In the last three years or so, we have worked very hard to stabilize the economy. Inflation has come as low as almost 2.7percent, but still went back to around 4.4 percent. We have stabilized the shilling, as you are aware,” the PS added. Kiptoo also encouraged Kenyans to invest in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, noting that investors who entered the stock market in recent years have more than doubled their investments due to improved market performance. “Macroeconomic stability has been achieved, and the stock market has performed exceptionally well. Those who invested have seen significant returns,” he said. Despite the gains, Dr. Kiptoo acknowledged that the government continues to face fiscal challenges, particularly in balancing revenue collection with rising public expenditure. “Everybody wants money, yet revenues are not growing as fast as our spending needs. This forces us to finance budget deficits. However, we remain committed to fiscal consolidation because it is in the country’s best interest to reduce debt and sustain economic stability,” he said. On the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, Dr. Kiptoo said Kenya has so far been shielded from severe economic impacts due to the resilience built over the past three years. “We have put in place measures to ensure the country continues to have adequate energy supplies despite the prevailing global uncertainties,” he added. PS Kiptoo also used the platform to appeal to Kenyans to remain united, saying national cohesion is essential for development. “We have a great country, and we have no other country but Kenya. Every time we face challenges, we overcome them because we are resilient. Let us continue promoting unity, love one another and work together for the good of our nation,” he said. His sentiments were echoed by Principal Secretary for the State Department for Forestry, Gitonga Mugambi, who urged Kenyans to uphold peace and patriotism. “We have a duty to love our country and take care of one another. Whatever our differences, we are one people and we are all Kenyans. We must ensure Kenya remains a country that we all cherish,” Mugambi said. The leaders were attending the burial of Josphat Simon Karinga Njagi the father of Dr. Jane Wangu Njuguna, Chief Executive Officer of the Kenya Forestry Research Institute (KEFRI). By Mutai Kipng’etich

Youth group turns one motorbike into thriving economic venture. A youth group in Ndhiwa East Sub-County has been hailed as a model of economic empowerment after transforming a single motorcycle into a diversified income-generating enterprise that now benefits dozens of its members. The Pala Moyie Boda Boda Youth Group received a major boost in 2018 when the then Ndhiwa MP, Augustino Neto Oyugi, donated one motorcycle to each of 22 youth groups under a youth economic empowerment programme. The group was among the beneficiaries. Speaking at Ojode Pala Trading Centre in South Kabuoch Location during a goat handover ceremony, the group’s Executive Secretary, Mark Onyango, said proceeds from the motorcycle business enabled the members to invest in three tents and a set of chairs, which they now hire out for community events such as weddings, funerals and meetings. The group later accumulated savings of about Sh268,000, allowing it to expand its investments. This week, members purchased 53 female goats and distributed them to 53 members as part of a livestock-rearing project aimed at improving household incomes. “While purchasing the goats, we could not get enough animals for all our members. We will later purchase the remaining 17 she-goats so that every member benefits from the initiative,” Onyango said. The former Ndhiwa MP, Augustino Neto Oyugi, who is also the co-party leader of the United Green Movement (UGM), praised the group’s prudent management of the resources they received. “When I first donated the motorbikes in 2018, I encouraged the 22 youth groups beneficiaries to use them to generate income. This particular group saved about Sh268,000 and invested in tents and chairs. They have now moved beyond collective investments to building the economic capacity of individual members by purchasing she-goats,” he said. Oyugi described the initiative as a significant milestone in youth empowerment and pledged continued support for the group. “This is a step in the right direction. We will continue working together with the group to ensure it has greater capacity to grow. We have also supported them with another motorcycle,” he said. He noted that youth empowerment and employment remain key pillars of the United Green Movement Party, adding that Kenya’s youthful population presents both an opportunity and a challenge. “Kenya has a youth demographic dividend, with nearly 70 per cent of the population aged between 18 and 35 years. Youth unemployment remains a serious challenge that requires all stakeholders to work together to address,” he said. Oyugi urged leaders across the country to invest in empowering young people instead of exploiting them for political violence. “Goonism is increasing because many young people are unemployed. As leaders, we must reject the use of youths for such vices and instead empower them with sustainable sources of income so they can live dignified lives,” he added. United Green Movement Party (UGMP) Co-organizing Secretary and Homa Bay County Woman Representative aspirant Elizabeth Ogweno commended the Pala Moyie Boda Boda Youth Group for discipline and resilience. “The Pala Moyie group has demonstrated discipline in management and resilience in the face of challenges. As leaders, we are committed to supporting development-oriented youth groups that are focused on improving the livelihoods of their members,” she said. By Sitna Omar

Title deeds restore hope to former Kihiumwiri land dispute victims. Residents of the former Kihiumwiri Land Buying Company settlement in Murang’a County are beginning a new chapter after decades of violent land disputes, following the Government’s land regularisation programme that has seen hundreds of title deeds issued to legitimate landowners. The exercise gathered momentum after Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome recently issued 750 title deeds to beneficiaries and directed a 90-day verification exercise to authenticate land ownership records before additional titles are processed. The settlement, now commonly known as Kenyatta Farm, was for years associated with violent land conflicts, prolonged court battles and disputed ownership claims that claimed lives, displaced hundreds of families and left many residents living in fear. Officials of Kihiumwiri Land Buying Company said the verification exercise is progressing well and is expected to be completed by the end of August, paving the way for the issuance of thousands of remaining title deeds. Company Director Josephat Thiongo said the exercise involves reconstructing historical land records to eliminate irregularities that had previously been exploited by land cartels. “We are rebuilding the registries to prevent any attempts to interfere with official records. This process will ensure that only genuine shareholders receive title deeds,” said Thiongo. He said completion of the verification exercise would enable the processing of the remaining title deeds and bring lasting certainty over land ownership in the settlement. According to company officials, the conflict claimed the lives of seven directors, while five others disappeared under mysterious circumstances and have never been traced. The violence also forced hundreds of families to flee their homes as disputes over land ownership intensified. Residents say the ongoing issuance of title deeds has restored confidence, reduced tensions and encouraged peaceful coexistence among people who were once divided by the conflict. Naomi Wanjiku, one of the beneficiaries whose husband was killed during the land clashes, described receiving a title deed as the end of years of uncertainty. “I am happy because I now know I will not be evicted from the land where I have lived for many years,” she said. She explained that residents are receiving title deeds for the parcels they currently occupy, while those whose original allocations correspond to undeveloped land retain ownership of those plots. The community is also seeking formal recognition of the name Kenyatta Farm in place of Kihiumwiri, saying the new identity symbolises reconciliation, peace and a fresh beginning after decades of violence, disappearances and prolonged legal battles over land ownership. By Muoki Charles

Youth urged to utilize ICT hubs for digital opportunities. Youth in Turkana have been urged to make use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) hubs in Lodwar to enhance their skills and tap into opportunities in the digital economy. Deputy County Secretary Joseph Nyanga made the appeal during a tour of ICT hubs in Lodwar, where he was accompanied by officials from the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF). Nyanga said the County Government will work closely with UNICEF through the Directorate of Vocational Training to address challenges affecting the smooth operation of the ICT hubs. He encouraged ICT hub operators to benchmark with successful service providers locally and internationally to improve the quality of services offered. The visit brought together officials from UNICEF and the county government, including Directorate of Vocational Training Director Stephen Eregae, his deputy Jeremiah Loyapan, and representatives from ICT, ECDE, partnerships, and vocational training centres. By Peter Gitonga

Kwale plants 2800 fruit tree seedlings to mark Mazingira day. By H, KNA Some 2800 fruit tree seedlings have been planted in Kwale county to mark this year’s Mazingira Day. The fruit tree planting exercise at Mavirivirini Primary School in Mwavumbo Ward, Samburu Sub-County of Kwale was led by Deputy Governor Chirema Kombo and County Commissioner (CC) Stephen Orinde. The countrywide tree planting campaign took place under the theme, “Citizen-Centric Tree Growing and Environmental Stewardship.” This year the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Forestry has urged all Kenyans to trace their primary school roots in a bid to donate and help in planting fruit trees on Mazingira Day marked annually on October10. The national government has set a target of 100 million fruit trees planted annually, translating into a budget of Sh1 trillion in 3 years. Deputy governor said the devolved government remains committed to protecting the environment and ensuring sustainable water for all. Kombo has urged area residents not only use the Mazingira Day to do tree planting, but also make it a habit of planting trees round the year. He highlighted the essential role trees play in absorbing carbon dioxide and protecting water catchment areas. “Since the national government directive of planting 15 billion trees by 2030 Kwale County has planted over 600,000 seedlings,” said Kombo. Speaking during the event, Chirema urged area residents particularly those from arid and semi-arid areas of Samburu, Kinango and LungaLunga sub counties to take the tree planting initiative seriously to curb the adverse climatic changes affecting the area. The DG noted the importance of tree planting in the arid and semi-arid zones adding that the initiative will help restore degraded land while improving livelihoods of local communities. “We have to change the narrative of our land and not just planting trees but growing fruit trees that will help us grow economically,” he said. On his part, Orinde said the national government works hand in hand with the county governments to make sure climate and environmental aspects are taken care of for the benefit of Kenyans. “The national government has many projects and we implement them together with the county government so that we change the harsh conditions for our people particularly in areas of Samburu Kinango and LungaLunga Sub-Counties,” he said. The CC urged residents to be intentional in planting and caring for tree seedlings, stressing that trees help in fighting climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. He said Kenya is facing an environmental crisis as a result of global warming, requiring collective action from all and sundry to combat the adverse effects of climate change. The CC explained that the choice of fruit trees by the government was deliberate, noting that besides their environmental benefits, they also provide a sustainable source of income for the people. “Let each one of us plant and nurture at least a tree not just for ourselves, but for our environment and posterity,” said Orinde.

Lodwar stormwater drainage project takes shape. Preparations for the implementation of the Lodwar Storm Water Drainage Project are underway, marking a significant step toward addressing flooding challenges within Lodwar Municipality. Pre-implementation activities, including technical engineering designs, Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA), and the development of a Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), are currently in progress. These activities commenced following the introduction of Avatech Consult Limited to the project site by Lodwar Municipality management and technical officers on 15th July 2026. Speaking during the site introduction, Municipality Manager, Peter Emuria, urged the consultant to adhere to the required quality standards and timelines outlined in the consultancy’s terms of reference. Project Engineer Augustus Keya highlighted the scope of the assignment and emphasized the importance of close collaboration between the consultancy team and municipal staff to ensure successful project delivery. Upon completion, the storm water drainage project is expected to significantly reduce the risk of flash floods, protecting households, businesses, infrastructure and livelihoods across Lodwar Municipality. Others present included Deputy Municipality Manager, Simon Nang’iro, Environment Officer John Kirwa, Accountant James Ekaran, Supply Chain Management Officer Gideon Kipyego, and technical personnel from Avatech Consult Limited. By Peter Gitonga

Busia to roll out Mpox vaccination campaign in Malaba. The County government of Busia is set to roll out an Mpox vaccination campaign in Malaba from July 17, 2026, in a 7–10-day exercise targeting populations at high risk of infection in the busy border region. The campaign is part of efforts to curb the spread of the disease in Teso North, which hosts the Malaba One Stop Border Post, one of Kenya’s busiest entry points. Malaba border post is characterized by high volumes of cross-border movement, increasing the risk of disease transmission. The exercise will target people who were not vaccinated during the previous campaign. Among those targeted are truck drivers, boda boda operators, sex workers, market vendors, hawkers, members of the cross-border business community, clearing and forwarding agents, hotel workers, money changers and frontline healthcare workers. Health officials will conduct both daytime and nighttime vaccination drives to ensure the targeted groups are reached at their places of work. Speaking during a stakeholders’ meeting, Teso North Sub-County Diseases Coordinator, Kelvin Tangara said each eligible person will receive a single dose of the vaccine and remain under observation for 30 minutes after vaccination to monitor any immediate adverse reactions. He added that vaccinated individuals will continue to be monitored for 28 days for any delayed adverse effects following immunization (AEFI). “We are also planning to roll out routine Mpox vaccination at the border point to reduce the risk of cross-border transmission of the disease,” he said. Tangara said every vaccinated person will receive a vaccination certificate as he urged residents to remain vigilant by observing preventive measures and seeking medical attention whenever they develop symptoms associated with Mpox. By Jane Kefrica and Elizabeth Achieng

Kapsabet gears up for Bishop Lelei installation. By L, KNA The Catholic faithful in Nandi are preparing for three days of prayer, ahead of the impending installation of Bishop John Kiplimo Lelei. The cleric is first Bishop of the newly created Kapsabet Diocese and the historic occasion has been scheduled for August 29 to 31. The festivities will open on 29th with a grand procession and vigil prayers at the Kapsabet Catholic Church. Choirs, youth groups, and women’s guilds will lead praise and worship sessions, as thousands gather to spiritually prepare for the ordination. The second day, will be the highlight, when Bishop Lelei is ordained and officially installed during a solemn Holy Mass at Eliud Kipchoge Sports complex in Kapsabet town. The mass will be presided over by the Apostolic Nuncio to Kenya Hurbertus Maria van Megen alongside the Archbishop of Eldoret Rev. Dominic Kimengich and bishops from across the country. The event is expected to attract thousands of Christians, clergy and leaders. On August 31, the faithful will conclude the celebrations with a thanksgiving service and cultural extravaganza, featuring traditional Nandi dances, youth choirs, and musical performances at St. Peters Catholic church in Kapsabet town. Leaders have pledged to support the new diocese both spiritually and socially. During a fundraising Mass on Sunday at Kapsabet Catholic Church, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula called for unity ahead of the historic installation. “The installation of Bishop Lelei is not just for Catholics; it is a blessing for the whole community. We call on everyone leaders and faithful alike to support the Diocese so that it may grow strong from the very beginning,” he said. The national assembly speaker commended the faithful for their perseverance and commitment saying, the creation of the Kapsabet Diocese is a testimony of faith and endurance. Nandi Governor Stephen Sang described Bishop Lelei’s appointment as a blessing for the County and vowed to fully support the church. “This installation is a unifying milestone for our people and a moment of pride for the entire Nandi community,” he said. Former Cabinet Minister Henry Kosgey, who was among the pioneers advocating for the creation of the new diocese, said the installation was the fruit of long prayers and persistence. “For decades, we petitioned the Vatican for a Diocese in Kapsabet. Today, our prayers have been answered, and future generations will benefit from a stronger presence of the church,” he said. Nandi Woman Rep Cynthia Muge lauded the moment as historic for women and youth. “The new diocese means more opportunities for our young people and women, who are the backbone of the church. Bishop Lelei’s leadership will ensure no one is left behind,” she said. Nandi Deputy Governor Dr. Yulita Mitei echoed the same sentiments, emphasizing inclusivity. “This Diocese will be a pillar not just of faith, but of community development. It will uplift families, empower the vulnerable, and give hope to generations,” added Mitei. Patrick Kitur, Moderator of the Eldoret Diocese, described the incoming Bishop as a devoted servant of God. “He has been a pillar of faith for decades, and this appointment is well deserved,” he said. The creation of the Kapsabet Diocese marks a major milestone for Catholics in Nandi and the wider Rift Valley. Until now, the faithful in the region were under the Diocese of Eldoret, which covered a vast geographical area stretching across several counties. The new Diocese will bring services closer to the people, ease pastoral work, and strengthen evangelization at the grassroots. It is also expected to spur the growth of Catholic-sponsored schools, health facilities, and community development projects in Nandi. Joseph Maiyo, a youth leader from Emgwen sub county said, “For a long time, our Diocese was too wide, and youth programs hardly reached us. Now we will have activities closer home that will nurture our talents and faith.” The 66 year old Bishop Lelei was born in Soy and has served the Catholic Church for over two decades. He was ordained in the early 2000s under the Diocese of Eldoret. He holds a Doctorate in Theology, specializing in liturgy, from the University of Vienna. He has served in various pastoral positions like Vicar in Suwerwa and Chepterit, as well as Parish Priest in Yamumbi, Tachasis, Kapcherop, Tindinyo, and Kapsabet He Studied philosophy at St. Augustine’s Senior Seminary (Mabanga) and theology at St. Thomas Aquinas Major Seminary (Nairobi) Lelei is widely respected for his pastoral approach, calm leadership style and commitment to grassroots evangelism and education He is celebrated for his deep liturgical knowledge, service in formation and seminary governance, as well as his pastoral dedication to families and youth. His appointment is seen as a milestone, ushering in localized spiritual leadership and growth in the Nandi region The installation and elevation of the Kapsabet Diocese is being hailed as both a spiritual triumph and a social milestone, with thousands expected to take part in the three-day celebrations.

Mombasa, SHOFCO partner to expand skills training opportunities. Mombasa County Government has partnered with Shining Hope for Communities (SHOFCO) to expand vocational skills training and economic empowerment opportunities for women and young people. Governor Abdulswamad Sheriff Nassir said his administration remains committed to improving access to education and creating pathways for residents to acquire practical skills that enhance livelihoods and promote self-reliance. The Governor spoke at Tononoka Grounds in Mvita Sub-County during SHOFCO’s community leadership elections presided over by the organisation’s Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Kennedy Odede. The exercise brought together hundreds of residents who elected officials to lead SHOFCO’s grassroots structures in Mombasa. Positions contested included chairperson, vice chairperson, secretary general, assistant secretary general, treasurer, youth representative, women representative, vice women representative, persons with disabilities representative, and minority representative. Addressing residents after the elections, Nassir said education and youth empowerment remain central pillars of his administration’s development agenda. He said the county government, in collaboration with the Mombasa County Assembly, had established a revolving fund to support vocational training for young people in various trades, including welding, tailoring, and masonry. The initiative is aimed at equipping young people with employable skills that enable them to secure livelihoods, start businesses, and create employment opportunities for others. “Our vision is to ensure that every young person has an opportunity to acquire practical skills that can improve their livelihoods. We want our youth to become job creators instead of job seekers, and that is why we continue investing in vocational training and empowerment programmes,” Nassir said. The Governor noted that the county had also implemented education support programmes to reduce the financial burden on families and encourage children to remain in school. He said the county’s school feeding programme targeting learners in Early Childhood Development Education (ECDE) centres and public secondary schools had helped ease pressure on parents by reducing education-related expenses. According to Nassir, the programme has enabled more learners to attend school consistently by supporting families struggling with rising costs of living. He added that the county government had introduced free ECDE education, supplied learning materials, and ensured ECDE teachers receive their salaries on time to improve the quality of early childhood education. On governance, Nassir praised SHOFCO for conducting a transparent, peaceful, and inclusive election, saying the process demonstrated that leadership contests can be conducted without divisions based on ethnicity, religion, or race. “The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission can draw valuable lessons from the SHOFCO elections. This process has shown that elections can be free, fair, and peaceful when transparency and unity are upheld,” he said. The Governor challenged SHOFCO to expand its civic education model to other counties ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying it would promote informed participation and strengthen peaceful democratic processes. He commended SHOFCO leadership and members for their continued efforts in empowering communities and creating opportunities for vulnerable groups. Nassir said the county government would continue partnering with organisations that prioritize citizen participation and community-driven development. Speaking during the event, Odede said SHOFCO believes sustainable development begins when communities are empowered to elect accountable leaders who understand and champion local priorities. He said the newly elected officials would serve as a link between residents and SHOFCO in implementing programmes focused on education, healthcare, livelihoods, and social welfare. Odede pledged to strengthen collaboration with the Mombasa County Government to expand vocational training, entrepreneurship programmes, and economic empowerment initiatives targeting women and youth. “Women and young people are the backbone of our communities. By equipping them with practical skills and creating opportunities for economic empowerment, we are building stronger families and a more prosperous society. We look forward to working closely with Governor Nassir to transform more lives in Mombasa,” Odede said. The Governor welcomed the partnership, saying collaboration between the county government and development partners such as SHOFCO would accelerate efforts to address unemployment, strengthen community resilience, and improve household incomes. The SHOFCO elections concluded peacefully, with residents expressing optimism that the newly elected leaders would strengthen community participation and support the implementation of development programmes across Mombasa County. By Joshua Peter

Money, religion threatens democratic process ahead of 2027 polls , warns NCCK. The National Council of Churches of Kenya (NCCK) has raised concerns over the growing influence of money and religion in shaping Kenya’s democratic process, warning that economic hardship is making many voters, particularly young people, more vulnerable to political manipulation ahead of the 2027 general election. Findings of a nationwide study released during a stakeholders’ forum in Kwale County indicate that vote buying, the politicisation of religious spaces and the recruitment of unemployed youth into politically sponsored violence are emerging as major threats to credible elections and democratic governance. The study, conducted across all NCCK regions through individual interviews and focus group discussions, was commissioned following the Gen Z-led protests against the Finance Bill to assess factors influencing citizens’ political choices and participation in democratic processes. Speaking during the release of the findings at PEFA Church in Kwale, NCCK Coast Region Chairperson Bishop Dr. Peter Mwero said financial inducements and religious influence continue to shape electoral decisions in many parts of the country, often at the expense of accountability and good governance. “Many citizens make electoral choices based on money or religious influence instead of leadership qualities and public interest. That weakens democracy and undermines good governance,” said Bishop Mwero. He noted that rising unemployment and economic hardships have left many young people susceptible to political exploitation, with some politicians allegedly using cash incentives to influence voters and recruit youth to disrupt political meetings. The cleric also expressed concern over the increasing use of places of worship as political platforms, saying some leaders attend religious events primarily to gain visibility and seek political support. “Places of worship should never become transactional spaces where donations are exchanged for political endorsement. The church must remain an independent moral voice that speaks for justice, truth and accountability,” he said. Mwero urged Kenyans to elect leaders based on integrity, competence and commitment to public service rather than short-term financial incentives. He further called for greater transparency and stronger oversight of campaign financing ahead of the 2027 polls. On political violence, the bishop condemned the recruitment of youth into organized gangs to disrupt political activities, warning that while politicians often reconcile after elections, communities are left grappling with long-term divisions and insecurity. “Youth should reject being used as instruments of violence and instead register as voters and participate peacefully in shaping the country’s future,” he added. Reverend Opondo Oluoch of the Anglican Church of Kenya (ACK), Diocese of Mombasa, and the youth representative in the NCCK Kwale County Coordinating Committee, challenged young people to make independent political decisions despite prevailing economic pressures. “As young people, we should not allow money to determine our vote. Our decisions must reflect the future we want for ourselves and for generations to come,” said Oluoch. He encouraged youth to pursue leadership opportunities and actively participate in governance processes instead of allowing themselves to be manipulated by politicians. Peninah Mwanyoha Ndegwa, Treasurer of the NCCK Kwale County Coordinating Committee and a member of the Methodist Church in Kenya, said the findings had reaffirmed the church’s responsibility to champion justice and good governance. “The church cannot remain silent when society is facing moral and governance challenges. We must continue guiding our communities to make informed decisions founded on truth and justice,” she said. Ndegwa called on churches to intensify civic education campaigns against vote buying, noting that women and young people remain among the groups most vulnerable to electoral bribery due to economic challenges. “The money offered during campaigns lasts only a day, but the consequences of electing leaders without integrity remain for years. Communities must resist exchanging their votes for temporary financial gain,” she said. She further urged the government to strengthen interventions aimed at reducing poverty and curbing voter bribery, arguing that addressing economic vulnerability would lessen politicians’ ability to influence electoral outcomes through cash handouts. The NCCK said the findings will inform future civic education and advocacy initiatives aimed at strengthening electoral integrity, promoting issue-based politics and encouraging informed voter participation as the country prepares for the 2027 General Election. By Chari Suche
